title: Reference lookup practice: identify required header, signature and valid inputs
learningObjectives: Explain the concept or reference contract.
Trace the example and justify its behaviour.
Identify relevant assumptions and edge cases.
Apply the skill in a documented exercise.

understand.concept: Effective reference lookup identifies the declaring header, exact prototype, parameter types, return type, preconditions, ownership rules and error indicators. A correct answer also checks the C version and implementation support.
understand.whyItMatters: This skill turns documentation into a practical engineering tool and reduces reliance on memorized but incomplete function descriptions.
understand.analogy: Treat a reference or learning task as a contract that states what is expected and how success is checked.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the exact C standard or library specification.

explain.narrative:
Effective reference lookup identifies the declaring header, exact prototype, parameter types, return type, preconditions, ownership rules and error indicators. A correct answer also checks the C version and implementation support.

Use authoritative declarations and documentation, state assumptions explicitly and verify behaviour with focused examples. Where the implementation or C version matters, record it.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: strtol is declared in stdlib.h. It returns long, uses endptr to report where parsing stopped and may set errno for range errors. The example also checks for unconsumed trailing characters.

practise.guidedTask: Find the strtol prototype and list each parameter's purpose.
practise.independentTask: For three library functions, create a reference card containing header, prototype, valid input, return and failure conditions.
hints: Do not rely only on a function's name; read its full contract.
Check whether the function is standard C or a platform extension.
Test both valid and invalid input cases.
